comparison_to_failed_native_run_37227042.interpretation: This diagnostic reproduced an unsafe CPU watch about 16.2 seconds after admission during the native side-panel startup route. It offers bracket attribution for that diagnostic interval, but the sampled panelReadyAt callback occurred 2.740 seconds after the unsafe watch, so the boundary refused before its bounded post-ready hold. The diagnostic does not establish the cause of the prior run's separate interval or acceptance behavior.

measurement_interpretation.known_owned_activity: Owned Chromium descendants accumulated 0.36 CPU-seconds and the owned Node process 0.03 CPU-seconds in the ps bracket; this is direct evidence that owned browser activity contributed during the bracket.
measurement_interpretation.provisioner: The host provisioner category delta was zero in the bracket. A later single CPU-percent snapshot is not interval attribution.
measurement_interpretation.unassigned_host_activity: Other host processes accumulated 1.69 CPU-seconds in the bracket. A post-bracket instantaneous process list showed two MTLCompilerServi processes at 83.7% and 48.3%; this cannot prove those processes generated the bracket's other-host delta or identify them as the runner provisioner.
measurement_interpretation.aggregate_comparison: The guard reported 0.87 busy on 3 CPUs, or roughly 2.61 aggregate CPU-seconds for its nominal one-second accounting row. The 2.08 CPU-second category sum comes from process snapshots that bracket the iostat command (1.083 seconds) but do not expose exact snapshot start/end times or exactly match that internal CPU row. The apparent difference is therefore only an approximate comparison, not a formal residual; ps is centisecond-quantized and exited/new/reparented/reused processes have unassignable CPU time.
measurement_interpretation.timing: The bracket begins and ends at the recorded iostat command boundaries, but iostat's one-second CPU row is an internal interval and the process snapshots enclose it rather than measuring precisely the same interval. Admission to unsafe watch was 16.211 seconds; panelReadyAt followed unsafe by 2.740 seconds. The native harness reached its exercise_panel stage, but the resource boundary refused retained unsafe history before the diagnostic completed its two-watch hold.
measurement_interpretation.unsafe_history: RESOURCE_WATCH_UNSAFE remains unsafe despite final resourceInvalid=false; final decision child_failed describes the child exit, not resource health.
measurement_interpretation.positive_conclusion: Owned Chromium and host-wide processes both had measurable CPU-time deltas while the guard sampled a high-CPU unsafe interval. This supports concurrent contribution, but does not establish which process class caused the threshold crossing, nor prove an environmental correction.
